Subject: Recap & plan: embeddings fit + drift checks for ClaritySearch POC

Hi Elise / Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Call highlights
- Primary use case: semantic search over customer support KB + cross-product docs (mix of short FAQs and long articles).
- Current pain: search returns many near-duplicates and struggles with product-specific synonyms; they see precision drop after a week of new docs.
- Success criteria: top-5 precision > 0.78 on our internal relevance set; average query latency < 60ms (embedding fetch + kNN approximate).

What Redwood will investigate (immediate POC plan)
1) Model candidates: run semantic-bench against two open/quantized candidates (symmetric and asymmetric experiments) — initial pick: open-embed-4096 and ridge-2b-384.
2) Dimensionality sweep: compare 384 vs 1024 dims and effect on kNN recall/precision vs storage cost.
3) Drift checks: run rolling simulated ingest for 30 days (synthetic) to measure representation shift and track centroid drift + query embedding drift metrics.
4) Prompt set / index config: share recommended prompt sets and similarity threshold guidance; include prompt-set CSV.

Deliverables and timeline
- By Wed (2026-03-11): semantic-bench PDF + prompt sets (attached).
- Thu (2026-03-12): short joint 60-min working session to walk through results and pick a model/config for a week-long live ingest test.

Attachments: clarity_poc_promptsets_v1.csv (prompt variants + exemplar queries)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/clarity/poc/embeddings-bench (benchmark tracking sheet), HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678

Ask from Clarity
- Please send a sample of ~5k docs and query logs (anonymized) if you want us to run on your real data; otherwise we will run synthetic drift tests first.

Next steps
- Elise: confirm whether we should use your sample data or proceed with synthetic.
- Redwood: prepare semantic-bench report + recommended model config.

Thanks — talk soon.

Hi Elise / Samir — thanks for the quick reply and the constraints; noted. I ran the first pass of semantic-bench on a synthetic dataset that mirrors your doc length distribution and query patterns. Attached: semantic-bench-results-20260310.pdf (summary + plots). High level findings below.

Quick TL;DR
- Best candidates: open-embed-4096 (384-d projection) and ridge-2b-384. open-embed-4096@384 had slightly higher top-5 precision (+0.04) but 2x storage vs ridge-2b-384.
- Dimensionality tradeoffs:
  * 384 dims: smaller footprint, recall drops on long-article queries about 3-4%.
  * 1024 dims: +0.06 precision on long-form but storage estimate exceeds your 150GB cap at current corpus size.
- Drift signals: centroid drift metric showed measurable shift after simulated weekly ingest equivalent to ~0.8% of vectors moving >0.15 cos distance; more pronounced for short-form docs.

Recommended next steps (technical)
1) If storage is fixed at 150GB, run a targeted 384-d + reranking approach: use 384-d ANN for candidate retrieval + cheap reranker (mini BERT) for top-20 re-ranking — gives precision benefits with modest storage.
2) If you can provision ~1.8x storage, try 1024-d open-embed variant for higher long-article quality.
3) Drift monitoring: instrument centroid and query-embedding drift dashboards (we can provide a Kibana template) and threshold alerts (suggested thresholds in the attached PDF).
4) Index refresh policy: recommend incremental reindex every 48 hours for high-ingest docs; full reindex weekly with sample holdout checks.

Bench notes & reproducibility
- Bench parameters and prompt variants are in clarity_poc_promptsets_v1.csv. The PDF includes exact model hashes, quantization mode, ANN config (HNSW parameters), and expected tokenization differences.

Action items
- Clarity: confirm whether Redwood should run the bench on your 5k sample (Elise said possible by EOD Wed).
- Redwood: if you confirm sample, we will run the bench on real data and re-share an updated PDF by Fri (2026-03-13).
- Schedule: propose Thu 2026-03-12 10:00am PT for a 60-min working session to review options and sign off on model/config.

Key links: semantic-bench results: https://drive.google.com/clarity/poc/embeddings-bench (sheet + raw outputs). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678
